chitchat: Nessa strops the razor twice, unhurried, and looks at your hairline like it owes her money.
"Wash first, then sit. I'm not cutting through that."
Steam rolls out of the arch at the back and fogs the mirror. Nessa wipes it without looking.
description: A barber with forearms like a rower's and a straight razor she strops while she talks, which is a conversational technique as much as anything. She has cut hair on this street for twenty years, through two sieges and one very bad winter, and takes the position that a man who has had a shave will make better decisions for at least a day.

root.text: "Baths are through the back and they're free, before you ask — I make my money on the hair, not the water." Nessa strops the razor twice. "Wash yourself, sit yourself down, and I'll make you look like someone who has a reason to be somewhere."

options.label: Twenty years on this street. Seen it change?
What do people talk about in the chair?

free.text: "The boiler's on whether you're in it or not. Costs me nothing to let you stand under it." She tests the razor's edge against her thumbnail. "And a man who's been washed buys a shave. A man who hasn't buys nothing and drips on my floor. It's not charity, it's plumbing with a business plan."

street.text: "When I started, the water came on for two hours a day and there was a queue round to Ironside." She shrugs. "Now it's on all day and the queue's the same length. People don't come for the water." A beat. "They come to be somewhere warm where nobody's asking them for anything."

gossip.text: "A man with a razor at his throat tells you the truth, and then tells you everyone else's."

bye.text: "Water's through the back. Take the towel, don't take the jar."

clothing_layers: a white barber's smock with a scorch mark she refuses to explain
a sleeveless undershirt and a leather strop looped at the belt

name: Nessa Marrit
